---
title: "Olympic Swimmers: Body Types Across Events and Eras"
author: "Omar Khater"
date: "September 2026"
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r}
#| label: height-trends
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5

library(tidyverse)

df <- read_csv("data/olympics.csv.gz", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(sport == "Swimming", year >= 1960, !is.na(height)) |>
  mutate(
    event_type = case_when(
      str_detect(event, "50 metres|100 metres") ~ "Sprint (50m/100m)",
      str_detect(event, "400 metres|800 metres|1,500 metres") ~ "Distance (400m+)",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    sex = if_else(sex == "M", "Men", "Women")
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(event_type))

df |>
  group_by(year, sex, event_type) |>
  summarize(mean_height = mean(height), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = mean_height, color = event_type)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~sex, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Olympic Swimmers Have Grown Taller, Led by Sprinters",
    subtitle = "Average height (cm) from 1960 to 2016 for Sprint vs. Distance freestyle events",
    x = "Olympic Year",
    y = "Average Height (cm)",
    color = "Event Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Across both men's and women's competitions since 1960, Olympic swimmers have grown taller over time, with sprinters consistently holding a height advantage over distance swimmers.
